content:
Look at this picture with me and imagine.

The spoiled lazy-bones pushed the unicorns too hard!
Together, they had spent hours trying to find a museum.
They wanted to become smarter.
The unicorns wanted to eat until they were full.
It was a warm day which had cool breezes,
like those under a demonstrative sociocracy.
The unicorns with their spoiled lazy-bones
on top cantered right past the museum.

There was something really lovely about the unicorns—
it was undeniable, even if they had been pushed too hard.

The procession hit the highway, cantering around the cars,
barriers and construction equipment. If you could think
of every possible way—and there are many—
that a thing with four spindles might canter down a highway
in a big woven group, you wouldn't pick this way.
You'd pick something simpler and more likely to return,
where the unicorn might move in an unmechanic
sulk towards the slung balance of volumes, as if to
take into account the empty belly of the animal.

This looked like a parade, but it wasn't.
They were actually trying to get somewhere.

One unicorn fell down because it was so tired.
It yelped, which made the spoiled lazy-bone on top feel sad.
title: Unicorns toiling
